claim: A small I-JEPA trained from scratch on an exact generated image world uses a visible class-colour key to predict the target latent of a fully masked object on pixel-distinct scenes sharing all twelve semantic templates. Correct context recovers object class, while a key-only cyclic replacement changes the prediction to the alternate key class while every other pixel remains fixed. Erasing the image-space key reduces accuracy to chance, zero latent context raises loss, and an untrained architecture remains at chance. A matched jointly optimized target ablation attains very low latent loss while compressing feature spread and weakening held-out prediction. Linear probes are explicitly not evidence here because random encoder features already decode this easy world. This is not an ImageNet or checkpoint-parity claim.
negative_result: Random features solve the easy probe. Seed 1 has effective rank 1.429 despite perfect causal recovery; effective rank alone neither proves nor rules out collapse.
interpretation: This is pixel-distinct evaluation of twelve shared templates, not natural-image or held-out semantic-template generalization.
